sermon.title: The Spirit of Prophecy Part 2
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer gives the marks of a real prophet, who stands in God’s counsel and speaks what the Bible says, and then teaches from 1 Chronicles 25, 2 Chronicles 20, 2 Kings 3 and Acts 16 about the anointing and the place of music and praise in prophecy and worship.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: in the 2 Kings 3 story he says “Elijah said also” where the prophet in the passage is Elisha; his wording is kept. He cites “2 Kings 3:14”; the request for a musician is in verse 15, so the whole passage is linked. Several Old Testament names were garbled in the captions and are written Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun and Jahaziel; a name near 6:31 and instrument names near 10:17 and 11:13 could not be made out and are marked [unclear]. He names two public religious figures in the first minute; those names are in the transcript only, not in the short answers. Near 22:51 he says God may “let Satan bring a plague of AIDS or whatever”; that is his own statement as spoken. Near 21:20 he answers the objection about God judging a nation; both are left as said.

chunks.section_question: What are the marks of a real prophet, and does it matter what other preachers say?
chunks.short_answer: He says the first mark is that “God did speak to them. God did send them,” and the second that “they did stand in His counsel”: they were people of the Word who read, studied and got into teaching where the Spirit revealed the Scriptures. He says they cause people to hear God’s words, and it does not matter what others say, “it’s what the Bible says.” When people say he thinks he is right and everyone else is wrong, he says, “I’m just telling you what the Bible says.”
chunks.text:
I want to give you the marks of a real prophet. They’re right here. Characteristic number one: God did speak to them. God did send them. Can I hear an amen? It’s right here, the opposite of the false. Characteristic number two: they did stand in His counsel. They were people of the Word. They found time to read and study the Word and get in teaching where the Word was being taught, not some book out of the Bible bookstore, but the Scriptures were being taught by the Holy Spirit revealing them. That’s the kind of people that are real prophets. “And they caused my people to hear my words,” not their words. See, it doesn’t matter what Copeland says, it doesn’t matter what the pope says, it’s what the Bible says.

Hallelujah. And I hear this all the time: “Well, you think you’re right and everybody else is wrong.” I didn’t say that. I’m just telling you what the Bible says. I’m not telling you what I say, I’m not telling you what I believe, I’m telling you what the Bible says. They probably put you on a guilt trip. “Well, how can all these people...” I hear this too: “How can all these people be wrong and you’re right?” I’m not telling you I’m right, I’m telling you what the Bible says. You show me in the Bible where you are right, and they can’t. They just believe some book, some tape, some CD, some guy off the TV.

chunks.section_question: What does he say the church is for, and who convicts people?
chunks.short_answer: He says the mark of a real prophet is that they “turn many people from their evil way,” and “that’s what the church is all about. It’s not about a social club.” He says no speaker has “the power to convict people”; a feel-good message is gone the next day, but “when they are touched by the Holy Ghost, He’s there the next morning.”
chunks.text: And number, item, characteristic number four: “They turn many people from their evil way and from the evil of their doings.” Folks, that’s what the church is all about. It’s not about a social club. It’s about us having our act together, so when people come, they are convicted by the Holy Spirit. They can reject Him (I see people reject), but they’re convicted by the Holy Spirit to turn from the wrong. And, folks, I don’t care how good a speaker you are, you don’t have the power to convict people. Oh, you might speak so well that they feel good at the moment, but the Holy Ghost is lasting, and you’re not lasting. When they go home and they get up the next day, that feel-good, inspired message is gone, but when they are touched by the Holy Ghost, He’s there the next morning saying, “Come on, boy. Come on, boy.”

chunks.section_question: How should the gifts of the Spirit be used?
chunks.short_answer: He says the Holy Spirit “needs a mouthpiece,” and “all of us can” prophesy one by one, speaking when you need to by the Holy Ghost, even one-on-one. He says the gifts are not a prize: “The gifts of the Spirit are weapons to use when we need them,” and the Holy Spirit will touch you at the time you need them.
chunks.text: Hallelujah. So us as a church, we need the Holy Spirit, don’t we? And we need the Holy Spirit speaking, and so that means He needs a mouthpiece, and all of us can, what? Prophesy one by one. In other words, you know, you can speak when you need to speak by the Holy Ghost. You might be talking to someone one-on-one, and the Holy Ghost will give you something to say, and you don’t have to say, “I got a word for you, for you,” that just puts a, that just makes you look good. That’s why you do that. “I have a word of God, God gave me a word for you.” Like the things of God are something that we go to the Olympics to win a prize about. “Oh boy, I got the prize of healing.” Oh, shut up. The gifts of the Spirit are weapons to use when we need them, and when you need them, the Holy Spirit will touch you and use that at the time. Can I hear an amen?

chunks.section_question: Did Paul have the gifts of the Spirit every day, and why does America need real prophets?
chunks.short_answer: He says Paul had all nine gifts but did not use them every day: in some cities God did no healing, and in others “God released the miraculous.” He says that when the Holy Ghost releases it, “you don’t get any credit,” and that God is bringing America low “so that we can get an ear to hear.”
chunks.text: Amen. Did Paul have all nine gifts of the Spirit? Yes, he did. Oh man, you’re looking at me like a “duh.” Did he use them every day? No. There were cities where he went into, God did no healing. He couldn’t turn that on: “Oh, I have the gift of healing.” He’d go from one city, he couldn’t do nothing in the miraculous; he’d go to another city, and God released the miraculous. And when the Holy Ghost releases, then you can do something, and you don’t get any credit. It’s the Holy Spirit. Hallelujah. Hallelujah. Now that’s the marks of a real prophet. Can I hear an amen? And, folks, we need in America some real prophets rising up. See, America’s, I mean, God is bringing us low in America so that we can get an ear to hear. You see His style all through the Bible. He has a style. We get up to the peak, and then we start forgetting how we got there, and then we start doing things on our own, and we start heading down.

chunks.section_question: What is an anointing, and why does music matter in God’s church? (1 Chronicles 25:1)
chunks.short_answer: He says real prophecy “speaks by the Spirit and gives nothing but scriptural facts.” From 1 Chronicles 25:1 he says an anointing is being “separated to service,” “a place where God does a ceremonial act to separate you for service,” and that David separated the Levites to prophesy with harps and cymbals. He says music is “a real key in God’s church, and He doesn’t need it. He chose to use it.”
chunks.text:
You know, we don’t get it. You know, economic problems come, health problems come, all this stuff comes. “Oh, we just believe God, hallelujah, you know, positive confession.” You know, we hit rock bottom like the guy in the pigpen, and then we come to our senses: “Okay, God, what do I need to do?” Then we get back up to the top of the mountain again. Real prophecy speaks by the Spirit and gives nothing but scriptural facts. Can I hear an amen? Nothing but scriptural facts. Now, I want to give you a quick example. Now, this is a very important part of this; you need to hear this. Okay, so open both ears. In 1 Chronicles 25:1 we read the story of David, David anointed or separated to service. Say “separated to service.” Separated service, that’s what an anointing is.

Okay, it’s a place where God does a ceremonial act to separate you for service. Okay, he separated the Levites here for service, and it’s very interesting. He took Asaph and his sons, Heman and his sons, Jeduthun [unclear] and his sons, to prophesy, speak, play by the inspiration, with harps, [unclear] and cymbals. Now, folks, this is vitally important. Music is a real key in God’s church, and He doesn’t need it. He chose to use it. Are you there? They could play by the inspiration of the Spirit on these instruments. They weren’t just up doing a little thing and, “No, no.” Just like Elijah spoke by the Spirit, these guys were playing by the Spirit.

chunks.section_question: Should the church use instruments, and where should kids learn music? (1 Chronicles 25:2-3)
chunks.short_answer: He says the world has “the wrong spirit of the music,” and that churches that allowed only a piano and an organ for decades is sad, because the Bible says they prophesied with harps, stringed instruments and cymbals. He says the sons of Asaph prophesied “according to the order of the king,” who is Jesus, and the sons of Jeduthun prophesied to give thanks and praise the Lord, “not flattering people.”
chunks.text:
Are you out there? You know, where do we send our kids to learn how to play music? To the world. Does the world know how to tune our kids in to the Spirit of the music? No, they got the wrong spirit of the music. They’re into the lust of the flesh, man. They’re into... See, the church is blindsided so much. Hallelujah. I know churches that wouldn’t allow anything but a piano and an organ for decades, and that’s sad, because the Bible said they prophesied with harps, stringed instruments (those are stringed instruments), and cymbals (that’s percussion). Amen. All right, the sons of Asaph, four, prophesied “according to the order of the king.” You see, who’s the king of the kingdom? Jesus. What order do we need to follow? His order. I don’t care what they’re doing out in the world. What is the Holy Ghost doing?

Church, I’m giving you some very good stuff here. I’m going to be dead and gone one of these days, and you need to have this in you so God can stir you. America needs to hear a real voice, and we need to take the responsibility to do it. The sons of Jeduthun, six, prophesied with a harp to give thanks and to praise the Lord. Praising who? The Lord. Not flattering people, giving honor to the Lord, giving honor to the Scriptures, teaching through music. And now remember, they were anointed back there, separated for service, right? Yes. Now look at this. Twenty years later Solomon comes along. It’s no more than 20 years, might be a little less, but anyway, 20 is a good figure here. Uh, I’ll tell you how I got there. David was old when he gave that separation. He lived, we don’t know how many years after he gave that separation. Solomon became king, and in the fourth year of his reign he built the temple of God and finished it in the 11th year, didn’t dedicate it till the 12th year.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asharelah; the sons of Asaph were under the direction of Asaph, who prophesied according to the order of the king.

Of Jeduthun, the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Shimei, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, six, under the direction of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with a harp to give thanks and to praise the LORD.

chunks.section_question: What happened at the temple dedication, and what orchestra did his church have? (2 Chronicles 5:12)
chunks.short_answer: He says that about 20 years later the Levites were “arrayed in white linen” with cymbals, harps and 120 priests sounding trumpets, and he says white linen is “righteousness of the saints.” He says his church in La Habra had a 27-piece orchestra that had to meet during the week, but “the results were staggering,” with the presence of God and conviction on people.
chunks.text:
Are you there? So we add 12 to whatever David lived, and about 20 years. Okay, 20 years have gone by. Now look what happened. They built the temple, they’re dedicating it. Now Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun, with their sons and brethren, “arrayed in white linen.” What’s white linen? Righteousness of the saints. We got to live right. We got to, you know, keep our repentance level up. We, amen, we got to keep admitting we’re wrong, not being stubborn. And they having cymbals, [unclear], harps, and 120 priests sounding with the trumpets. Now we got the wind instruments. Back in the Vine in La Habra, we had a 27-piece orchestra. Okay, it had violas, it had violins, it had cellos, piccolo, flutes, harp.

We had a percussion section, we had a guitar, we had a bass, string bass and electric bass, okay. We had a flugelhorn, he said, “[unclear]?” We had an [unclear]. And let me tell you, you couldn’t come an hour before service and get ready with a 27-piece orchestra. You had to meet during the week, you had to pull this thing together, and you had to teach that electric guitar to quieten down when we needed to hear the stringed instruments, and you had to teach the string instruments, “Just lay your instruments down and just enjoy the high praises,” because the electric and the percussion and certain instruments just do the high praise, they just do it. Are you there? And so you got all these hassles, but boy, the results were staggering, weren’t they? The presence of God and the conviction on people, and God moving them and breaking them down, was powerful.

chunks.short_answer: He says no one loses it by feelings: “You’re separated for service,” and “the anointing has nothing to do with your feeling. The feeling will come when you participate in what you’ve been set apart to do.” He says worship should have a message, with a place for comfort, strengthening and souls being saved, and “it worked, because the Holy Ghost come and added His ingredient to it.”
chunks.text:
“The trumpeters and singers were as one to make one sound in praising and thanking the Lord.” And when they did, and they sang this song, “For He is good, for His mercy endures forever,” “the glory of the Lord filled the house.” See, results came. Now, 20 years went by. Did they lose their anointing? Well, that’s what I hear all the time: “I’ve lost my anointing.” How do you lose an anointing? You’re separated for service. You know, some woman comes up to me and offers sex to me (this has happened over and over in my life). Am I supposed to lose my anointing because I don’t feel like saying no? Do you go by feelings, or do you go by what you’ve been selected to serve in? And you’re selected to serve in what? Holiness and righteousness. Are you there?

See, I don’t have to feel like it. “Well, I don’t feel like I got anything.” The anointing has nothing to do with your feeling. The feeling will come when you participate in what you’ve been set apart to do. Wow, that was good. Man, I’ve heard people say, “Well, I lost the anointing.” How do you lose serving Jesus? You’ve been set apart to serve Jesus and living a right life. You’ve been set apart to praise Him, worship Him, play instruments under Him. You know, maybe you don’t feel like it today. I didn’t feel like getting up and going to work every day. How many of you can raise your hand and say, “Yeah, I ain’t...” That’s the last thing I wanted to do, but I did it, because that was my responsibility. And once I got to work and got moving, I, man, everything was fine.

And that’s the way it is here, folks. In the Pentecostal Spirit-filled circles, we say things that are just stupid. “Well, my anointing is molded, you know, like bread. You know, it’s old and molded and hard. I need a fresh anointing.” Jesus said, “I’ll baptize you with the Holy Ghost and fire.” Have you ever seen fire get molded? You ever seen a fire that got stale? Where is our thinking? We are set apart, and music is very important. Music in the church, the worship service, is just as important as the message that’s going to follow or the message before it, because worship should have a message, because we learned that prophecy is for what? Our learning, our comfort. There should be a place in the worship for comfort. There should be a place for strengthening. There should be a place for souls to be saved. What’s the words up there? It worked, because the Holy Ghost come and added His ingredient to it.

scriptures.text_nkjv: indeed it came to pass, when the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking the LORD, and when they lifted up their voice with the trumpets and cymbals and instruments of music, and praised the LORD, saying: “For He is good, For His mercy endures forever,” that the house, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud, so that the priests could not continue ministering because of the cloud; for the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.
I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance, but He who is coming after me is mightier than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.

chunks.section_question: How did God fight for Israel when the singers went out? (2 Chronicles 20)
chunks.short_answer: He says the Spirit came on a Levite “in the middle of the congregation,” and God put the singers in front of the army, and “when they began to sing and to praise the Lord, God set ambushes against the enemy.” He says God began moving “at the beginning of their singing,” and he adds that he doesn’t like private prophecies, since “two or three prophesy and the other judge.”
chunks.text: Now, 100 years later the old guard is dead. The fathers who David anointed is gone. The new generation has come up. Jahaziel, a Levite, the son of Asaph, came on him, came the Spirit of the Lord, in the middle of the congregation. And that’s very important, these private prophecies. I’m getting more agitated every year I get older. You know, if we’re going to do something, we should do it in the presence of people, so they, how can two or three prophesy and the other judge if they’re not around to judge your nonsense? And let me tell you, I hear a lot of nonsense anyway. When they began, when he spoke and they, the army, the singers went out and began to sing praises, how many, you know, that is not a good idea for our military to go over to Iraq and start singing praises. We go over with our weapons. But when God is involved, that’s His weapon. He put the singers in front of the army, and listen to this: when they began to sing and to praise the Lord, God set ambushes against the enemy. When did God start moving against the enemy? At the beginning of their singing. And so they’re marching out there and they’re singing, “Great is the Lord, His mercy endureth forever,” and they’re marching, and these singers are going, “Oh man, we’re getting closer and closer, somebody better do something.” They didn’t know that God already started the ambush, and when they got there, the army had turned on one another, killed one another, and all they had to do is get the spoil. But it started when? At the beginning.

And he said, “Listen, all you of Judah and you inhabitants of Jerusalem, and you, King Jehoshaphat! Thus says the LORD to you: ‘Do not be afraid nor dismayed because of this great multitude, for the battle is not yours, but God’s. Tomorrow go down against them. They will surely come up by the Ascent of Ziz, and you will find them at the end of the brook before the Wilderness of Jeruel. You will not need to fight in this battle. Position yourselves, stand still and see the salvation of the LORD, who is with you, O Judah and Jerusalem!’ Do not fear or be dismayed; tomorrow go out against them, for the LORD is with you.” And Jehoshaphat bowed his head with his face to the ground, and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem bowed before the LORD, worshiping the LORD. Then the Levites of the children of the Kohathites and of the children of the Korahites stood up to praise the LORD God of Israel with voices loud and high. So they rose early in the morning and went out into the Wilderness of Tekoa; and as they went out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, “Hear me, O Judah and you inhabitants of Jerusalem: Believe in the LORD your God, and you shall be established; believe His prophets, and you shall prosper.” And when he had consulted with the people, he appointed those who should sing to the LORD, and who should praise the beauty of holiness, as they went out before the army and were saying: “Praise the LORD, For His mercy endures forever.” Now when they began to sing and to praise, the LORD set ambushes against the people of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir, who had come against Judah; and they were defeated.
Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others judge.

chunks.section_question: Is the anointing for music and prophecy passed on to the next generation?
chunks.short_answer: He says he asks us to see that “that separation to the service of the Lord in music and in prophecy just keeps being passed on to the next generation by God.” He says you don’t have to say “if I only had so-and-so’s anointing”; you have to accept it and “begin,” and “they didn’t have to feel it.”
chunks.text: See, if God can just get us started. You understand the illustration. If He could just get us to start, we will see great things, the kingdom of darkness destroyed. Now remember, we just taught out of Ezra and Nehemiah. That’s, it’s, uh, 400 years later. Asaph, and that anointing is still there. All these guys are gone, the forefathers, the next one, the next one, everybody’s gone. It passed on. What am I trying to tell you? That separation to the service of the Lord in music and in prophecy just keeps being passed on to the next generation by God. You don’t have to say, “Boy, if I only had so-and-so’s anointing, boy, if I only had so-and-so’s gift of God.” No, no, no. Jesus is passing it on to the next generation, but you got to accept it, and you got to begin. What’s the two words? It worked. See, they didn’t have to feel it. They didn’t have to say, “I lost the anointing, it’s been years since God moved.” They just began again to do what they were separated to do, and God moved, and joy filled the place, and they sent gifts unto them for whom nothing was prepared. Great things happened in Ezra and Nehemiah.

chunks.section_question: Why did Elisha ask for a musician? (2 Kings 3)
chunks.short_answer: He says that when the army was dying of thirst, Elisha said, “Bring me a musician.” He says Elisha had done mighty things without one, but “here he had the sense to know he needed the musicians,” and after they played by the Spirit of God he got a word: dig ditches, because water would come the next day.
chunks.text: Second Kings 3:14. Jehoshaphat is king, the army, the army went out to fight, and there’s no water. The army is dying from thirst, and when an army is dying from thirst, they’re going to lose the battle. So they went to Elisha the prophet, and Elisha the prophet said, “Bring me a musician.” Now, this really illustrates the power of music in the kingdom. Elisha had prophesied many a time without a musician, am I right? He had done mighty things without a musician, but here he had the sense to know he needed the musicians to come, the prophets that could play by the Spirit of God. And so they brought him the musicians, they began to play by the Spirit of God, and then he got a word from God how the thirst was going to be quenched. He said, “Go out and dig ditches. There’s going to be water coming from nowhere tomorrow. Tomorrow, not going to be any rain, not going to be any wind, they just going to be water. Dig some ditches, channel this water, because it’s coming.” So they went out and dug the ditches, and the next day, sure enough, the water came from Edom, their enemy. God took their water and brought it to Israel. Are you there?

scriptures.text_nkjv: And Elisha said, “As the LORD of hosts lives, before whom I stand, surely were it not that I regard the presence of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not look at you, nor see you. But now bring me a musician.” Then it happened, when the musician played, that the hand of the LORD came upon him. And he said, “Thus says the LORD: ‘Make this valley full of ditches.’ For thus says the LORD: ‘You shall not see wind, nor shall you see rain; yet that valley shall be filled with water, so that you, your cattle, and your animals may drink.’ And this is a simple matter in the sight of the LORD; He will also deliver the Moabites into your hand. Also you shall attack every fortified city and every choice city, and shall cut down every good tree, and stop up every spring of water, and ruin every good piece of land with stones.” Now it happened in the morning, when the grain offering was offered, that suddenly water came by way of Edom, and the land was filled with water.

chunks.section_question: How does he answer, “How can God be God when He judges a whole nation?”
chunks.short_answer: He says the enemy saw the water as blood, and “it all depends on what side of God you’re on.” To the objection about killing women and children, he says, “He’s God, and He’s the judge of the world, and when He judges a nation or a people… that’s His business.”
chunks.text: Ah, is that how you read your Bible? Don’t you think you need to start reading your Bible like I’m telling you? Yeah, took the enemy’s water, brought it down supernaturally, ran into that valley. They had the ditches, the water was channeled through the valley, the soldiers could drink, and Elijah said also, “God is going to give you this battle with Moab and Edom. You’re going to win the battle.” And so the Moabite army, they had heard that Israel was coming, so they went out to fight them, and the water to them looked like blood. You see, it all matters what side of God you’re on, how you see things. It all depends on what side of God you’re on. See, Israel saw water, and they were drinking and getting their thirst quenched. The enemy saw blood, and they go, “Hey, the kings have turned on themselves, they’re all dead, we’ll just go and reap the spoil,” and they went right into a trap. Israel just annihilated it, women, children, and all. And my opponent say, “How can God be a God when He says to kill women, children, and all?” Listen, He’s God, and He’s the judge of the world, and when He judges a nation or a people and says, “Listen, it’s going to cost every one of your life,” that’s His business. Don’t be telling me my God is a bad God because He does His job.

And they said, “This is blood; the kings have surely struck swords and have killed one another; now therefore, Moab, to the spoil!” So when they came to the camp of Israel, Israel rose up and attacked the Moabites, so that they fled before them; and they entered their land, killing the Moabites.

chunks.section_question: Can music drive out an evil spirit? (1 Samuel 16:23)
chunks.short_answer: He says David and Saul were both Holy Spirit anointed, but Saul never repented, so God sent a troublesome spirit upon him “trying to get his attention,” and when David played his harp the spirit would depart. He says “music has a power over the witchcraft, the sorcerers, the kingdom of darkness.”
chunks.text: Amen. If He decides to let Satan bring a plague of AIDS or whatever to straighten things out, don’t you blame my God. My God is doing what His job is to do. First Samuel 16:23: “The evil spirit from God was upon Saul.” David, who was Holy Spirit anointed, played a harp. Saul, who was Holy Spirit anointed, but he never repented. Do you understand that both of these two men were Holy Spirit anointed, both of them filled with the Holy Ghost? But Saul never repented of his sins. David did. And so God sent an evil spirit, a troublesome spirit, upon Saul, trying to get his attention, and when David would play with his harp, the spirit would what? Depart. You see, music has a power over the witchcraft, the sorcerers, the kingdom of darkness in this world. Just music will drive them out.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And so it was, whenever the spirit from God was upon Saul, that David would take a harp and play it with his hand. Then Saul would become refreshed and well, and the distressing spirit would depart from him.

chunks.section_question: What does he say about witchcraft abroad and the “blood over my door”?
chunks.short_answer: He says in third world countries most witchcraft is “fleshly witchcraft,” and that people have said “there’s fire over your door.” He says he has the blood of Jesus over his door, as the blood protected the dwellings in Egypt, and “they can’t touch me.”
chunks.text:
And, folks, when I go to third world countries, you know, the sorcery, the witchcraft is very strong over there. Most of it is fleshly witchcraft, it’s not demonic at all. And, you know, when I’ve been in these nations and I confront these people, they will say a statement like, I’ll say, “Well, you know, come on, bring it on, do something to me. You guys got power, come on, do something, put a wart on my nose, you know, but don’t touch me.” You just curse me, you just put a spell on me, you know, “come on, do something, make me a leper, whatever, come on, bring it on.” This is what they’ll say: “There’s fire over your door.” Are you there? He will fill you with the Holy Ghost and fire.

You see, and let me tell you, there’s blood over my door too. I don’t have to have the fire, I got the blood. I mean, you know, when the Satan came through, the death angel at Egypt, he couldn’t go into those dwellings with the blood over their door. I got the blood of Jesus over my door, I got the fire over my door, they ain’t messing with me, and they’ll admit it. They were demonic, and they could see, without them knowing I’m a Christian, they could see they can’t touch me. Now we got a thousand years later, Paul and Silas are in prison, and at midnight they began to sing praises unto God. The anointing hasn’t worn off, it hasn’t gotten stale, and it hasn’t been lost. It’s still there because it’s God’s anointing.

chunks.section_question: How were Paul and Silas freed from prison by singing? (Acts 16)
chunks.short_answer: He says Paul and Silas sang praises at midnight, “the anointing hasn’t worn off,” and a great earthquake opened the doors and loosed everyone’s bands “simply because they sang praises to God.” He says they had only their voices and “God set the captive free,” as in the words “the Spirit of the Lord is upon me.”
chunks.text: And when they did that, the prisoners heard them. They weren’t praying and singing silently. You silent saints need to open your mouth up. It’s the sound that comes from your lip that God uses to fight the kingdom of darkness. Suddenly a great earthquake shook the foundations of the prison, and immediately all the doors were open and everyone’s bands were loosed, simply because they sang praises to God. They didn’t have any instrument here, couldn’t take them into the prison with them, but they had their voices. They couldn’t clap their hands because they were in shackles, but they had their voices, and God set the captive free, exactly what He said He would do in Isaiah and in the Gospels: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, for He has anointed me,” set me apart for service, “to preach the gospel to the poor, to set the captive free, to open the blinded eyes, to open the prison doors to them that are bound.” That’s exactly what God fulfilled right there, a thousand years later. That anointing was still working.

Suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken; and immediately all the doors were opened and everyone’s chains were loosed.

“The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon Me, Because the LORD has anointed Me To preach good tidings to the poor; He has sent Me to heal the brokenhearted, To proclaim liberty to the captives, And the opening of the prison to those who are bound; To proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD, And the day of vengeance of our God; To comfort all who mourn,

“The Spirit of the LORD is upon Me, Because He has anointed Me To preach the gospel to the poor; He has sent Me to heal the brokenhearted, To proclaim liberty to the captives And recovery of sight to the blind, To set at liberty those who are oppressed; To proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD.”

chunks.section_question: What is the bottom line, and when does God start moving?
chunks.short_answer: He asks, “Do we want the testimony of Jesus in our life and in our church?” and says no one has a right “to take part of the Bible and leave the rest out.” He says real people will come “to the water because they’re thirsty” and “to the fire because they’re cold,” and that God starts moving the minute we begin.
chunks.text:
So the bottom line is this: do we want the testimony of Jesus in our life and in our church? Will we follow the guidelines and say nothing and do nothing except what is limited to us in the Scriptures? Do any of us have a right to take part of the Bible and leave the rest out? No one does, not just ministers, but ministers are going to be judged for it. Seriously, seriously, and I don’t want to get up there and have to face that. Man, if a church has Jesus, what will it have operating? The spirit of prophecy, speaking, playing, our music, our worship anointed, the Spirit moving upon it, touching people’s lives. Yes, they can reject God, they rejected Jesus, but that does not give us an excuse to water down the Word, reduce the Word in any way. We have to hang tight and let Jesus begin to bring them in, because I guarantee you real people will come to the water because they’re thirsty. Real people will come to the fire because they’re cold. See, fire attracts the cold, water attracts the thirsty, and food attracts the hungry, and I’m talking about spiritual water, the Holy Ghost, spiritual food, the Word of God, and spiritual fire.

And remember, He starts moving when we begin. He doesn’t wait for us to get mature. The minute we make a move toward Him, He starts working. Now, we won’t see the result for a while. We got to keep marching, but when we get down there, we’re going to see the result of what He started to do when we started to do our part.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And I fell at his feet to worship him. But he said to me, “See that you do not do that! I am your fellow servant, and of your brethren who have the testimony of Jesus. Worship God! For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.”

faqs.question: What is the first mark of a real prophet?
faqs.answer: He says it is that “God did speak to them. God did send them,” the opposite of the false prophets.

scriptures.text_nkjv: “I have not sent these prophets, yet they ran. I have not spoken to them, yet they prophesied. But if they had stood in My counsel, And had caused My people to hear My words, Then they would have turned them from their evil way And from the evil of their doings.

faqs.question: Does it matter what famous preachers and religious leaders say?
faqs.answer: He says no: “it doesn’t matter what” they say, “it’s what the Bible says.”

faqs.question: Is he saying he is right and everyone else is wrong?
faqs.answer: He says no: “I’m not telling you I’m right. I’m telling you what the Bible says.” He says “you show me in the Bible where you are right, and they can’t.”

faqs.question: Can a good speaker convict people?
faqs.answer: He says no: “I don’t care how good a speaker you are, you don’t have the power to convict people.” He says the Holy Ghost is lasting and a feel-good inspired message is gone the next day.

faqs.question: Should you announce “I have a word from God for you”?
faqs.answer: He says you can speak when the Holy Ghost gives you something to say, even one-on-one, and “you don’t have to say, ‘I got a word for you,’” since that “just makes you look good.”

faqs.question: Did Paul use all nine gifts of the Spirit every day?
faqs.answer: He says Paul had all nine but “no”: in some cities “God did no healing,” and he “couldn’t turn that on.” In other cities “God released the miraculous.”

faqs.question: What does it mean to be anointed?
faqs.answer: He says to be anointed is to be “separated to service,” and that it is “a place where God does a ceremonial act to separate you for service.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Moreover David and the captains of the army separated for the service some of the sons of Asaph, of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who should prophesy with harps, stringed instruments, and cymbals. And the number of the skilled men performing their service was:

faqs.question: Does he say the church should only use a piano and organ?
faqs.answer: He says no: churches that wouldn’t allow anything but a piano and an organ for decades is sad, “because the Bible said they prophesied with harps, stringed instrument… and cymbals. That’s percussion.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Moreover David and the captains of the army separated for the service some of the sons of Asaph, of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who should prophesy with harps, stringed instruments, and cymbals. And the number of the skilled men performing their service was:

faqs.question: What did it take to have a 27-piece orchestra?
faqs.answer: He says you couldn’t come an hour before service and get ready; you “had to meet during the week.” He says there were hassles but “the results were staggering,” with “the presence of God and the conviction on people.”

faqs.question: How do you lose an anointing?
faqs.answer: He says, “How do you lose an anointing? You’re separated for service.” He says you don’t go by feelings but by what you have been selected to serve in: holiness and righteousness.

faqs.question: Does the anointing depend on how you feel?
faqs.answer: He says no: “The anointing has nothing to do with your feeling. The feeling will come when you participate in what you’ve been set apart to do.”

faqs.question: Can the anointing get “moldy” or stale?
faqs.answer: He says some people say “my anointing is molded,” but Jesus said He would baptize you with the Holy Ghost and fire, and he asks, “have you ever seen fire get molded? You ever seen a fire that got stale?”

scriptures.text_nkjv: I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance, but He who is coming after me is mightier than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.

faqs.question: Why does he say prophecy should be done in front of people?
faqs.answer: He says, “if we’re going to do something, we should do it in the presence of people,” because “how can two or three prophesy and the other judge if they’re not around to judge your nonsense?”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others judge.

faqs.question: When did God start moving against the enemy?
faqs.answer: He says it was “at the beginning of their singing.” He says the singers did not know that “God already started the ambush,” and the army they faced had turned on one another.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel the son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, a Levite of the sons of Asaph, in the midst of the assembly. And he said, “Listen, all you of Judah and you inhabitants of Jerusalem, and you, King Jehoshaphat! Thus says the LORD to you: ‘Do not be afraid nor dismayed because of this great multitude, for the battle is not yours, but God’s. Tomorrow go down against them. They will surely come up by the Ascent of Ziz, and you will find them at the end of the brook before the Wilderness of Jeruel. You will not need to fight in this battle. Position yourselves, stand still and see the salvation of the LORD, who is with you, O Judah and Jerusalem!’ Do not fear or be dismayed; tomorrow go out against them, for the LORD is with you.” And Jehoshaphat bowed his head with his face to the ground, and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem bowed before the LORD, worshiping the LORD. Then the Levites of the children of the Kohathites and of the children of the Korahites stood up to praise the LORD God of Israel with voices loud and high. So they rose early in the morning and went out into the Wilderness of Tekoa; and as they went out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, “Hear me, O Judah and you inhabitants of Jerusalem: Believe in the LORD your God, and you shall be established; believe His prophets, and you shall prosper.” And when he had consulted with the people, he appointed those who should sing to the LORD, and who should praise the beauty of holiness, as they went out before the army and were saying: “Praise the LORD, For His mercy endures forever.” Now when they began to sing and to praise, the LORD set ambushes against the people of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir, who had come against Judah; and they were defeated.

faqs.question: What happened when Paul and Silas sang in prison?
faqs.answer: He says “a great earthquake shook the foundations of the prison, and immediately all the doors were open and everyone’s bands were loosed, simply because they sang praises to God.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: But at midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them. Suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken; and immediately all the doors were opened and everyone’s chains were loosed.
